records.title: VQ35HR Oil Consumption
records.description: The VQ35HR engine in the EX35 exhibits higher-than-normal oil consumption, typically burning 1 quart every 2,000-3,000 miles. Worn valve stem seals and piston ring coking contribute to the problem, especially in vehicles with infrequent oil changes.
records.solution: Perform an oil consumption test at the dealer to establish baseline usage. Replace valve stem seals if consumption exceeds 1 quart per 1,500 miles. Use quality 5W-30 synthetic oil and change every 5,000 miles.
symptoms: Light blue exhaust smoke on startup

records.title: VQ37VHR Timing Chain Noise
records.description: The VQ37VHR engine in the QX70 can develop timing chain rattle, especially on cold starts. The primary timing chain stretches and the tensioner cannot fully compensate, resulting in a distinctive metallic rattle that typically quiets after 10-30 seconds.
records.solution: Replace the timing chain, tensioners, and guides as a set. Use updated Nissan timing chain components with improved tensioner design. Ensure regular oil changes with quality synthetic oil to minimize chain wear.
symptoms: Check engine light for cam timing

records.title: Transfer Case Output Seal Leak
records.description: AWD-equipped FX/QX70 models develop transfer case output shaft seal leaks, allowing gear oil to seep onto the exhaust and create a burning smell. The seals harden and crack from heat exposure over time.
records.solution: Replace the transfer case output seals and inspect the transfer case fluid level. Refill with genuine Nissan transfer case fluid. Check the driveshaft joints for wear while the transfer case is accessible.
symptoms: Oil drip from center of vehicle

records.title: Brake Rotor Warping / Front Brake Vibration
records.description: Infiniti service bulletin ITB00-024I applies to all Infiniti vehicles and defines brake judder as vibration felt through the vehicle, steering wheel or brake pedal while braking. The bulletin identifies rotor thickness variation and/or rotor runout as the cause; brake-pedal pulsation and, in severe cases, steering-wheel oscillation can result.
records.solution: Verify the condition with the driver and a road test. Infiniti directs technicians to correct brake judder by machining the rotors with an approved on-car brake lathe. If a rotor is replaced, index it to the axle hub for minimum runout, tighten lug nuts evenly with a torque wrench, and burnish serviced brakes as specified in ITB00-024I.

records.description: The FX35 commonly develops intermittent failures of the camshaft position sensors and sometimes the crankshaft position sensor, causing stalling, hard starts, or limp operation. Heat and age degrade the sensor electronics, and this issue is widely reported across Nissan/Infiniti VQ applications of the era.
records.solution: Diagnosis is done by scanning for correlation or sensor circuit codes and monitoring live RPM/cam signals during crank and road test. Repair usually involves replacing one or both cam sensors and sometimes the crank sensor, preferably with OE-quality parts because low-cost sensors often cause repeat faults. Typical repair cost is about $150-$450 depending on how many sensors are replaced and labor rates.

records.title: Front Suspension Clunk / Worn Control Arm Bushings
records.description: The FX35 is well known for front-end clunks, loose steering feel, and uneven tire wear caused by worn front lower control arm bushings, compression rod bushings, and sway bar end links. The vehicle's weight and sporty suspension tuning accelerate bushing wear, especially on rough roads and higher-mileage examples.
records.solution: Diagnosis involves checking for play in the lower control arms, tension/compression rods, ball joints, and sway bar links while the suspension is loaded. Repair usually means replacing the worn arm assemblies or bushings and then performing a four-wheel alignment. Typical cost is about $300-$1,000 depending on whether one side or multiple front suspension components are renewed.

records.title: Radiator Crack and Coolant / Transmission Cross-Contamination
records.description: On first-generation FX35 models with the automatic transmission cooler integrated into the radiator, internal radiator failure can allow coolant and ATF to mix. Owners report radiator tank cracking or internal cooler failure, which can quickly damage the transmission if not caught early.
records.solution: Diagnosis includes checking the radiator and overflow bottle for oily residue, inspecting ATF for a milky appearance, and pressure-testing the cooling system. Repair typically requires replacing the radiator and thoroughly flushing the cooling and transmission systems; if contamination was severe, transmission repair or replacement may also be needed. Costs range from about $400 for early radiator replacement to $5,000+ if the transmission has been damaged.

records.title: Steering Wheel Lock Malfunction
records.description: The electronic steering wheel lock mechanism can malfunction, preventing the car from starting or causing intermittent no-start conditions. The steering lock actuator motor fails internally, triggering a security fault.
records.solution: Replace the steering lock actuator or have the dealer reprogram the BCM. Some owners bypass the lock mechanism entirely, though this may affect resale value. A TSB was issued for certain model years.

records.title: Power Window Regulator Failure
records.description: The power window regulators in the G35 are prone to failure, causing windows to fall into the door or operate slowly. The plastic guide clips and cable mechanism wear out, especially in hot climates.
records.solution: Replace the window regulator assembly. Aftermarket regulators are available at lower cost than OEM. The repair involves removing the door panel and disconnecting the window motor.

records.title: Concentric Slave Cylinder Failure (Manual)
records.description: Manual transmission G37s suffer from premature concentric slave cylinder (CSC) failure. The internal seal degrades, causing clutch fluid to leak into the bell housing and resulting in a soft or sinking clutch pedal.
records.solution: Replace the concentric slave cylinder, which unfortunately requires transmission removal. Many owners upgrade to an aftermarket CSC with improved seals. Flush the clutch hydraulic system after replacement.

records.title: Oil Gallery Gasket Leak
records.description: The VQ37VHR engine develops oil leaks from the oil gallery gaskets located between the upper and lower oil pans. Oil seeps onto the exhaust, creating a burning smell and potential fire hazard if left unaddressed.
records.solution: Replace the oil gallery gaskets, which requires removing the lower oil pan. Use updated Nissan/Infiniti gaskets that have improved sealing material. Clean all mating surfaces thoroughly before reinstalling.
symptoms: Burning oil smell from engine bay
Visible oil seepage on lower engine block

records.title: Electronic Steering Lock Failure

records.title: Forward Emergency Braking (FEB) Phantom / False Activation
records.description: Owners of the QX55 and platform-mate QX50 report the Forward Emergency Braking / Intelligent Emergency Braking system activating with no obstacle present, including hard braking while passing large trucks, coasting under bridges and overpasses, or on certain road surfaces. FEB can engage even with ProPILOT Assist off. Unexpected automatic braking in traffic is a rear-end-collision hazard. A related TSB notes the AEB warning light can blink in heavy rain/fog or when the windshield lane camera window is contaminated.
records.solution: Keep the front camera window (behind the windshield) and front radar/emblem area clean and free of film, mud, snow or aftermarket tint. Have the dealer scan the ADAS modules and apply any camera/radar calibration or software update per TSB. If phantom braking persists, request a diagnosis of the radar/camera alignment; the FEB sensitivity setting can be reviewed but the system should not be defeated permanently.
symptoms: Automatic braking with no obstacle present
Hard braking under bridges/overpasses or passing trucks

records.title: Infotainment System Freezing
records.description: The QX55 infotainment system experiences periodic freezing, slow boot times, and wireless Apple CarPlay disconnections. The system occasionally requires a manual reboot to restore functionality during driving.
records.solution: Update to the latest infotainment firmware. Perform a factory reset if issues persist. Delete and re-pair all Bluetooth devices. Infiniti has released multiple software updates addressing stability.

records.title: Premature 12V Battery Failure / Parasitic Drain (No-Start, Warning Cascade)
records.description: The 2022 QX55 debut year drew numerous complaints of the 12V battery failing to hold a charge or discharging prematurely, leaving the vehicle with a no-crank/no-start condition, key-detection errors and a cascade of dashboard warning messages at startup. In one reported case a battery-related electrical failure led to a sudden loss of power steering assist, a serious safety concern. Parasitic draw from the vehicle's electronics and short-trip driving accelerate the problem.
records.solution: Load-test the battery and charging system; replace with a correct OEM-spec Group 35/AGM battery if degraded. If the battery drains while parked, perform a parasitic-draw test to isolate a module (infotainment/telematics) staying awake. Reprogram/replace the battery and register it if the system requires. Address any charging (alternator) fault and keep the battery topped up on a maintainer during long storage.
symptoms: Multiple dashboard warning messages at startup
Reported loss of power steering assist with electrical failure

records.title: VC-Turbo Engine Main/Link Bearing Failure (Safety Recall)
records.description: Nissan issued a large 2026 recall covering VC-Turbo four-cylinder vehicles including the Infiniti QX55, QX50 and Altima. Under certain operating conditions the engine can experience high oil temperatures that degrade lubrication of the crankshaft main bearing and the A-, C- and L-link bearings of the variable-compression mechanism. In the worst case a bearing seizes or a failed bearing breaches the engine block, causing catastrophic engine failure. This is a distinct defect from the previously documented oil-consumption issue. Nissan also announced a VC-Turbo warranty extension. Symptoms often precede failure and out-of-warranty engine replacements have run five figures.
records.solution: Have the VIN checked for the recall. The remedy reprograms the ECM, scans for diagnostic codes, and inspects the oil pan for metal debris; if metal is found the engine is replaced free of charge. Owners should keep to strict oil-change intervals, use the correct 0W-20 spec oil, and stop driving immediately if knocking, ticking or metal in the oil is noticed. Because a warranty extension applies, keep all service records to protect coverage.

records.title: VC-Turbo Engine Oil Consumption
records.description: Like the QX50, the QX55 with the VC-Turbo KR20DDET engine exhibits elevated oil consumption. The variable compression mechanism creates additional oil consumption pathways, and owners report needing top-offs between the 5,000-mile service intervals.
records.solution: Monitor oil levels bi-weekly and top off with 0W-20 synthetic. Follow the Infiniti oil consumption test procedure if usage exceeds 1 quart per 3,000 miles. Warranty coverage may apply for excessive consumption.
symptoms: Oil level dropping 1+ quart per 3,000 miles

records.title: Battery Drain / No-Start from Telematics, Infotainment, or Control Module Sleep Issues
records.description: Owners of the redesigned QX60 have reported dead batteries, repeated jump-starts, and no-start conditions after the vehicle sits overnight or for a few days. Complaints and forum reports point to parasitic draw from modules that do not go to sleep properly, including telematics and infotainment-related systems, rather than a simple worn battery in many low-mileage cases. The problem is especially frustrating because battery replacement alone may not permanently fix it.
records.solution: Perform a proper parasitic draw test after all modules should be asleep, then isolate the circuit causing excess current draw. Check for TSB/software updates for telematics/AV modules, test battery health, and inspect charging system output; some vehicles need module reprogramming, while others require battery replacement after repeated deep discharge damage. Document draw readings before replacing parts.
symptoms: Dead battery after sitting overnight or a few days
No crank or clicking on startup

citations.title: NHTSA complaints for 2022-2025 Infiniti QX60 battery drain / no-start

communityRecommendations.content: Ask for a parasitic draw test printout instead of accepting a battery swap as the only diagnosis.
If the vehicle sits often, a smart maintainer can prevent deep discharge while the root cause is being diagnosed.

records.title: CVT Transmission Failure
records.description: The Jatco CVT in the QX60 is prone to premature failure, particularly in the 2013-2017 models. The transmission overheats during towing or sustained highway driving, leading to shuddering, slipping, and eventual complete failure.
records.solution: Replace CVT fluid every 30,000 miles instead of the recommended 60,000. Add an auxiliary transmission cooler for towing. Nissan extended the CVT warranty to 84 months/84,000 miles on affected models.

records.title: Forward Collision Warning / Automatic Emergency Braking False Activation or Unexpected Braking
records.description: Owners have reported unexpected forward collision warnings and abrupt braking events with no obvious obstacle ahead, especially in traffic, on curves, or near roadside objects. These complaints are tied to the QX60's ADAS sensor/camera interpretation rather than a conventional brake hardware fault. Sudden braking can create a rear-impact hazard and is one of the more serious owner-reported safety concerns on the current generation.
records.solution: Scan the ADAS system for stored faults and verify radar/camera alignment, windshield condition, and front emblem/radar cleanliness. Infiniti service procedures typically involve checking for software updates, recalibrating the forward camera/radar, and replacing a faulty sensor only after alignment and aiming are confirmed. Owners should document the exact conditions when the event occurs to help reproduce the issue.
symptoms: Forward collision warning with no vehicle ahead
Dash warning messages for FEB/AEB or front sensor

citations.title: NHTSA complaints for 2022-2025 Infiniti QX60 involving false braking / FCW-AEB behavior

communityRecommendations.content: Keep the front emblem/radar area and windshield camera area clean; contamination can worsen false alerts.
After windshield replacement or front-end work, insist on proper ADAS calibration rather than assuming the system will self-learn.

records.title: Panoramic Moonroof Exploding or Cracking Spontaneously
records.description: A number of current-generation QX60 owners have reported the panoramic glass roof suddenly cracking or shattering with a loud bang while driving, often without any clear impact evidence. Complaints commonly describe the inner shade catching falling glass and the damage appearing to originate upward, consistent with tempered glass breakage rather than a direct rock strike. While not universal, the reports are repeated enough to be a known owner concern on the redesigned model.
records.solution: Inspect the glass carefully for impact point evidence and document the break pattern before replacement. Repair requires replacing the affected moonroof glass panel and checking frame alignment, seal fitment, and drain condition; if there is no impact evidence, owners should pursue warranty/goodwill review and file a safety complaint. Avoid driving with exposed broken glass until the panel is secured or replaced.
symptoms: Loud popping or gunshot-like noise from roof

citations.title: NHTSA complaints for 2022-2024 Infiniti QX60 panoramic sunroof shattering

communityRecommendations.content: Take photos of the glass pattern before cleanup; owners report this helps when disputing a denied warranty claim.
Use OEM glass and have the shop verify drain routing and frame alignment during replacement.

records.title: Power Steering Pump Whine
records.description: The hydraulic power steering pump develops a pronounced whining noise, especially during cold starts and low-speed turning. Air intrusion into the power steering fluid or a failing pump bearing causes the noise.
records.solution: Flush the power steering system and refill with Nissan PSF. Bleed air from the system by turning the wheel lock-to-lock several times with the engine running. Replace the pump if the noise persists after fluid service.

records.title: Rearview Camera Image Blank, Distorted, or Intermittent Due to Infotainment/Display Software
records.description: Multiple owners of the redesigned 2022+ QX60 reported the backup camera showing a black screen, frozen image, delayed image, or distorted view when shifting into reverse. This is safety-significant because the rearview image may not display as required, and Infiniti/Nissan issued a recall covering certain vehicles for software that can cause the center information display not to show the rearview camera image. Owner complaints describe intermittent failures that may temporarily clear after a restart but recur unpredictably.
records.solution: Confirm the concern by checking for intermittent camera loss, delayed display, or frozen image when selecting reverse. Inspect for open recalls and apply the latest AV/control unit software update per Infiniti/Nissan service procedure; if the issue persists, diagnose the display control unit, camera harness, and rear camera module for faults or poor connections. Vehicles still under recall/warranty should have the software remedy performed first.
symptoms: Black screen when shifting into reverse
Rear camera image delayed or frozen
Distorted or blank center display image
Issue may clear after key cycle and return later

records.title: Transmission Judder at Low Speed
records.description: The QX60 CVT exhibits a pronounced judder during low-speed maneuvers such as parking lot driving and stop-and-go traffic. The torque converter and CVT belt interaction produces an uncomfortable vibration through the drivetrain.
records.solution: Have the dealer perform the CVT judder reprogram (TSB NTB15-024). A CVT fluid change with NS-3 fluid can also improve the condition. Drive the vehicle for 30 minutes after the fluid change to allow the TCM to relearn.

records.title: Hydraulic Body Motion Control System Leak
records.description: The QX80 equipped with Hydraulic Body Motion Control (HBMC) develops fluid leaks from the hydraulic actuators and lines. The system uses high-pressure hydraulic fluid to control body roll, and seal degradation leads to leaks and reduced effectiveness.
records.solution: Inspect and replace leaking hydraulic lines and actuator seals. The HBMC fluid reservoir should be checked regularly. Complete system replacement is expensive but may be necessary if multiple components have failed.

records.title: Infotainment System Slow Response
records.description: The QX80 infotainment system exhibits noticeable lag when navigating menus, inputting destinations, and switching between audio sources. The aging hardware platform cannot keep pace with modern connected car expectations for a luxury SUV.
records.solution: Update to the latest available firmware. Reduce the number of paired Bluetooth devices. The 2025+ models received an updated system, but earlier models remain limited by hardware constraints.

records.title: VK56VD Timing Chain Stretch
records.description: The 5.6L VK56VD engine can develop timing chain stretch, particularly when oil changes are neglected. The primary and secondary timing chains elongate over time, causing rough idle, reduced power, and potential engine damage if not addressed.
records.solution: Replace the timing chain, tensioners, and guides as a complete kit. This is a labor-intensive repair requiring significant engine disassembly. Strict adherence to 5,000-mile oil change intervals helps prevent premature chain wear.
symptoms: Check engine light with timing codes
